work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Galatas
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

2.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : DEINDE POST ANNOS QUATUORDECIM, ETC.
2.title_en: Elucidation of the second chapter: Then, after fourteen years, etc.

paras.t: DEINDE, expleta prædicatione in Syria atque Cilicia, post annos quatuordecim a Christi passione, in quibus includuntur tres anni prædicti a Pauli conversione, post quos prius venit Jerusalem, iterum ascendi a terris humilioribus Jerosolymam, dum quæstio erat de legalium observatione (prout in Actibus plenius enarratur), cum Barnaba ex Judæis converso, assumpto et Tito ex gentilitate converso : quatenus horum testimonio comprobarem, falsam esse assertionem dicentium me aliud Judæis, aliud gentibus prædicare. Ascendi autem, non meo decreto, sed secundum revelationem Christi mihi ostensam. Et contuli cum illis Jerosolymitis evangelium quod prædico in gentibus, id est, de prædicatione et doctrina evangelica quam annuntio gentibus, habui tractatum cum illis, generaliter tamen et quasi superficialiter. Seorsum autem, id est in privato, separatim, contuli particulariter et profunde cum his qui videbantur veraciter aliquid esse, id est ceteris præstantiores ac doctiores : per quos intelligit Petrum, Jacobum et Joannem, sicut patebit post pauca. Ideo autem contuli, ne forte in vacuum, id est infructuose, quantum ad auditores, currerem, prædicando Evangelium Dei, aut cucurrissem frustra. Prædicatio nempe apostoli Pauli multis erat suspecta, quia cum Christo in carne conversatus non fuit, nec cum ceteris Apostolis Spiritum Sanctum recepit, nec inter Apostolos diu fuerat conversatus. Ideo propter securos reddendos alios, necessarium sibi fuit Jerosolymam ire et cum Apostolis loqui, ut eorum auctoritate sua prædicatio roboraretur. Unde quod ait, Ne forte, etc., non sic est intelligendum quasi Apostolus aliquo modo ambigeret de suæ prædicationis veritate ; sed ad aliorum æstimationem refertur, quibus prædicatio Pauli non profuisset, nisi cum aliis contulisset Apostolis.
paras.en: [[2:1|Then|Deinde]], having finished his preaching in Syria and Cilicia, [[2:1|after fourteen years|post annos quatuordecim]] from the passion of Christ (in which are included the three years mentioned above from Paul's conversion, after which he first came to Jerusalem), [[2:1|I went up again|iterum ascendi]] from lower lands [[2:1|to Jerusalem|Jerosolymam]], when the question about the observance of the legal ceremonies was raised (as is more fully told in the Acts)[[Acts 15:4||]], [[2:1|with Barnabas|cum Barnaba]], converted from among the Jews, [[2:1|taking Titus also|assumpto et Tito]], converted from the Gentiles: so that by their testimony I might prove false the assertion of those who said that I preach one thing to the Jews and another to the Gentiles. [[2:2|And I went up|Ascendi autem]], not by my own decision, but [[2:2|according to revelation|secundum revelationem]] of Christ shown to me. [[2:2|and communicated to them|Et contuli cum illis]], the people of Jerusalem, [[2:2|the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles|evangelium quod prædico in gentibus]]: that is, I held discussion with them about the gospel preaching and doctrine which I announce to the Gentiles, yet in general and as it were on the surface. [[2:2|but apart|Seorsum autem]], that is, in private, separately, I conferred in detail and in depth [[2:2|to them who seemed to be some thing|cum his qui videbantur veraciter aliquid esse]] in truth, that is, those more eminent and more learned than the rest: by whom he means Peter, James and John, as will appear shortly. And I conferred for this reason, [[2:2|lest perhaps I should run or had run in vain|ne forte in vacuum]], that is, fruitlessly as far as my hearers were concerned, [[2:2|I should run|currerem]], preaching the Gospel of God, [[2:2|or had run|aut cucurrissem]] to no purpose. For the preaching of the apostle Paul was suspect to many, since he had not lived with Christ in the flesh, nor received the Holy Ghost with the other Apostles, nor spent long among the Apostles. Therefore, to reassure others, it was necessary for him to go to Jerusalem and speak with the Apostles, so that his preaching might be strengthened by their authority. Hence his words, Lest perhaps, etc., are not to be understood as though the Apostle doubted in any way of the truth of his preaching; they refer rather to the opinion of others, to whom Paul's preaching would have been of no profit had he not conferred with the other Apostles.

paras.t: Ostenso quod doctrina Pauli ab Apostolis commendata sit, ostenditur quod facta ejus laudata sint. Sed neque Titus, qui mecum erat in Jerusalem, quum esset gentilis ex utroque parente, nam Græcus erat, compulsus est a veris Apostolis circumcidi : quamvis aliqui ex Judæis conversi, præcipue Pharisæi, niterentur ad hoc : non enim idonea erant motiva eorum. Cur ergo vos, Galatæ, circumcisionem recipitis? Sed propter subintroductos falsos fratres, id est propter quosdam simulatores Judæos, hæreticos, vel omnino in Judaismo induratos, qui callide inducti fuerunt ad nostram societatem sub specie religionis a pseudoapostolis, qui falsi fratres subintroierunt nostrum conventum, explorare, id est observare et experiri, libertatem nostram, id est exonerationem ab observantiis cæremonialium legis, quam habemus in Christo Jesu, id est virtute et merito Christi, qui nos ab onere tanto absolvit merito suæ dignissimæ passionis, in qua figuralia impleta sunt et finem sumpserunt. Introierunt ergo non recta intentione, sed ut nos in servitutem legis, id est ad observantias legales, redigerent : quod erat onus adeo grave, quod neque patres nostri, neque nos ferre potuimus. Propter hos ergo restitimus : secundum quod subditur :
paras.en: Having shown that Paul's doctrine was commended by the Apostles, he shows that his deeds were approved. [[2:3|But neither Titus, who was with me|Sed neque Titus, qui mecum erat]] in Jerusalem, [[2:3|being a Gentile|quum esset gentilis]] on both sides (for he was a Greek), [[2:3|was compelled|compulsus est]] by the true Apostles [[2:3|to be circumcised|circumcidi]], although some converted Jews, especially Pharisees, strove for this; for their motives were not sound. Why then, Galatians, do you accept circumcision? [[2:4|But because of false brethren unawares brought in|Sed propter subintroductos falsos fratres]]: that is, because of certain dissembling Jews, heretics, or men altogether hardened in Judaism, who were craftily brought into our company under a show of religion by false apostles; [[2:4|who came in privately|qui falsi fratres subintroierunt]] into our assembly [[2:4|to spy|explorare]], that is, to watch and test, [[2:4|our liberty|libertatem nostram]], that is, our release from the observances of the ceremonies of the law, [[2:4|which we have in Christ Jesus|quam habemus in Christo Jesu]], that is, by the power and merit of Christ, who freed us from so great a burden by the merit of his most worthy passion, in which the figures were fulfilled and came to their end. So they came in with no right intention, but [[2:4|that they might bring us into servitude|ut nos in servitutem redigerent]] of the law, that is, to the legal observances: which was a burden so heavy that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear it[[Acts 15:10||]]. Because of these, then, we resisted; as follows:

paras.t: Quibus neque ad horam, id est nullo temporis spatio, cessimus hac vice in Jerusalem subjectioni, id est ad hoc ut nos suæ voluntati aut legalium observationi subjicerent, ut veritas Evangelii, id est doctrina novæ legis, quæ docet cessasse legalia, permaneat apud vos, id est, in cordibus vestris firma et fixa consistat. Adversariis namque veritatis et fidei resistendum est rationabiliter, dum fides seu veritas periclitaretur : et talis resistentia non pertinet ad impatientiam, sed justitiam.
paras.en: [[2:5|To whom|Quibus]] [[2:5|no, not for an hour|neque ad horam]], that is, for no space of time, [[2:5|we yielded not|cessimus]] on this occasion in Jerusalem [[2:5|by subjection|subjectioni]], that is, so as to let them subject us to their will or to the observance of the legal ceremonies, [[2:5|that the truth of the gospel|ut veritas Evangelii]], that is, the doctrine of the new law, which teaches that the legal ceremonies have ceased, [[2:5|might continue with you|permaneat apud vos]], that is, may stand firm and fixed in your hearts. For the adversaries of truth and faith are to be resisted with reason when faith or truth is endangered; and such resistance belongs not to impatience but to justice.

paras.t: Ab his autem, hoc est præ falsis fratribus istis, qui videbantur esse aliquid, id est majorem sapientiam et auctoritatem possidere, videlicet veri Apostoli, Petrus, Jacobus et Joannes, quales, id est quam illitterati, pauperes, abjecti et modici, aliquando fuerint, antequam a Christo vocati erant, imo usque post ejus resurrectionem. Petrum namque et Joannem piscatores fuisse certissimum est. Ideo nihil mea interest, id est, ad me non pertinet de hoc magnam facere mentionem, ne videar eos contemnere, aut me ipsum jactare, qui ante conversionem mei, doctus et dives, potens et nobilis eram, utpote natus civis Romanus. Ideo etiam ad me non pertinet illud narrare, quia nec obest nec prodest : nam Deus personam hominis non accipit, id est, propter hæc naturalia et accidentalia exteriora, non præfert unum alteri, sed propter dona divina et merita. Unde non obest illis quod tales fuerunt, nec ideo sunt spernendi. Hinc etiam in Actibus Apostolorum adstruit Petrus : In veritate, inquiens, comperi quod non est personarum acceptor Deus. Nullum enim ad se redeuntem contemnit vel abjicit. Verumtamen, ideo Paulus recitat ista, ut Galatæ sciant eum non esse ignarum legalium, sed quantum ad humanam pertinet instructionem, prædictis Apostolis fuisse eruditiorem. Unde constat quod ab eis edoctus non sit.
paras.en: [[2:6|But of them|Ab his autem]], that is, rather than these false brethren, [[2:6|who seemed to be some thing|qui videbantur esse aliquid]], that is, to possess greater wisdom and authority, namely the true Apostles Peter, James and John: [[2:6|what they were|quales]], that is, how unlettered, poor, lowly and small, [[2:6|some time|aliquando fuerint]], before they were called by Christ, indeed until after his resurrection. For it is quite certain that Peter and John were fishermen[[Matt 4:18||]][[Matt 4:21||]]. Therefore [[2:6|it is nothing to me|nihil mea interest]], that is, it is not my business to make much mention of this, lest I seem to despise them or to boast of myself, who before my conversion was learned and rich, powerful and noble, being born a Roman citizen[[Acts 22:27||]]. It is not my business to tell it, also because it neither harms nor helps: for [[2:6|God accepteth not the person of man|Deus personam hominis non accipit]], that is, he does not prefer one to another on account of these natural and accidental outward things, but on account of divine gifts and merits. So it does them no harm that they were such, nor are they to be despised for it. Hence Peter too affirms in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 10:34|in very deed I perceive that God is not a respecter of persons|In veritate, inquiens, comperi quod non est personarum acceptor Deus]]. For he despises or casts off none who returns to him. Yet Paul recounts these things so that the Galatians may know that he was not ignorant of the legal ceremonies, but, as far as human instruction goes, was more learned than these Apostles. Hence it is clear that he was not taught by them.

paras.t: Denique, demonstrato quod nihil in sua doctrina correxerunt, nunc manifestat quod nihil in ea suppleverunt. Mihi autem qui videbantur esse aliquid, id est prædicti magni Apostoli, nihil contulerunt de sapientia. Nam quidquid ab illis audivi, ante cognovi ex revelatione divina. Sed econtra, id est contra opinionem adversariorum meorum, quum vidissent Apostoli isti quod creditum est mihi evangelium præputii, id est, quod mihi a Christo commissa esset prædicatio evangelica gentibus incircumcisis proponenda, sicut et Petro creditum est evangelium circumcisionis, id est prædicatio Judæis inferenda : non quod evangelia ista sint diversa aut alia, sed unum evangelium diverse nominatur propter diversitatem hominum quibus impenditur. Qui enim operatus est Petro in apostolatum circumcisionis, id est Christus qui Petro commisit officium apostolatus sui exercere in populum Judæorum, eos docendo et convertendo, operatus est et mihi inter gentes, id est, gentilium apostolum me constituit, et efficaciam inter eos mihi largitus est. Unde Dominus : Vas, inquit, electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram gentibus ; et alibi ad Paulum, Vade, quia ad gentes longe mittam te. Hæc quoque non sunt intelligenda præcise, sed appropriate. Non enim sic dicitur Petrus Judæis missus, quasi non sit missus ad gentes : imo per eum primo conversi sunt Cornelius centurio, et qui cum eo erant gentiles. Nec sic Paulus dicitur missus ad gentes, quasi non sit missus ad Judæos : sed sicut in Actibus legitur, ipse et Barnabas longo tempore prædicaverunt solis Judæis. Sed ideo ista dicuntur, quia præcipue erat Petro commissa conversio Synagogæ, Paulo autem gentilitatis conversio. Judæi quippe signa, Græci autem sapientiam quærunt. Petrus ergo qui in signis præfulsit, ad Judæos congrue missus est : Paulus vero, in sapientia singularis, missus est Græcis. Non tamen simpliciter præferenda videtur sapientia Pauli, sapientiæ Archiapostoli.
paras.en: Finally, having shown that they corrected nothing in his doctrine, he now makes plain that they added nothing to it. [[2:6|for to me they that seemed to be some thing|Mihi autem qui videbantur esse aliquid]], that is, those great Apostles, [[2:6|added nothing|nihil contulerunt]] in wisdom. For whatever I heard from them I knew before by divine revelation. [[2:7|But contrariwise|Sed econtra]], that is, contrary to the opinion of my adversaries, [[2:7|when they had seen|quum vidissent]], these Apostles, [[2:7|that to me was committed the gospel of the uncircumcision|quod creditum est mihi evangelium præputii]], that is, that the gospel preaching to be set before the uncircumcised Gentiles had been committed to me by Christ, [[2:7|as to Peter|sicut et Petro]] was committed the gospel [[2:7|of the circumcision|circumcisionis]], that is, the preaching to be brought to the Jews: not that these gospels are different or other, but the one gospel is named differently by reason of the difference of the men to whom it is given. [[2:8|For he who wrought in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision|Qui enim operatus est Petro in apostolatum circumcisionis]], that is, Christ, who committed to Peter the office of exercising his apostleship among the Jewish people, teaching and converting them, [[2:8|wrought in me also among the Gentiles|operatus est et mihi inter gentes]], that is, made me apostle of the Gentiles and granted me efficacy among them. Hence the Lord says: [[Acts 9:15|this man is to me a vessel of election, to carry my name before the Gentiles|Vas, inquit, electionis est mihi iste, ut portet nomen meum coram gentibus]]; and elsewhere to Paul: [[Acts 22:21|Go, for unto the Gentiles afar off will I send thee|Vade, quia ad gentes longe mittam te]]. These things also are not to be understood exclusively but by appropriation [[that is, as ascribing to each what belongs to him chiefly, not solely]]. For Peter is not said to be sent to the Jews as though he were not sent to the Gentiles: indeed by him first were converted Cornelius the centurion and the Gentiles who were with him[[Acts 10:1||]]. Nor is Paul said to be sent to the Gentiles as though he were not sent to the Jews: rather, as we read in the Acts, he and Barnabas for a long time preached to the Jews alone[[Acts 13:2||]][[Acts 14:1||]]. But these things are said because to Peter was chiefly committed the conversion of the Synagogue, and to Paul the conversion of the Gentiles. [[1 Cor 1:22|For both the Jews require signs: and the Greeks seek after wisdom|Judæi quippe signa, Græci autem sapientiam quærunt]]. So Peter, who shone forth in signs, was fittingly sent to the Jews; Paul, singular in wisdom, was sent to the Greeks. Yet the wisdom of Paul does not seem to be preferred absolutely to the wisdom of the chief Apostle.

paras.t: Et quum cognovissent gratiam, id est virtutem miraculorum et sapientiæ affluentiam, prædicationisque præstantiam atque aptitudinem, quæ data est mihi, Jacobus Alphæi, frater Domini, et Cephas, id est Petrus, et Joannes evangelista, qui videbantur, id est, certo sciebantur et cernebantur, columnæ esse, id est sua perfectione aliorum imbecillitatem sustentare, Ecclesiam stabilire, et omnibus præfulgere, dexteras dederunt mihi et Barnabæ societatis, id est, ad suam societatem nos receperunt, atque in signum sodalitatis et apostolicæ communionis dexteras suas nostris dexteris inseruerunt, ut nos in gentes prædicaremus, ipsi autem in circumcisionem, id est inter Judæos. Tantum, id est, hoc solum adjecerunt, ut pauperum memores essemus, qui omnia sua vendentes, pretium posuerunt ante Apostolos, et postea fame exorta, in magna penuria fuerunt. Unde Apostoli rogaverunt Paulum et Barnabam, ut gentes conversas hortarentur ad succurrendum istis pauperibus. Quod etiam sollicitus fui hoc ipsum facere, id est hanc commissionem effectui commendare, inducendo gentiles ad mittendum eleemosynas his egenis. Patet namque in diversis epistolis, quam sollicitus fuerit Paulus pro collectis. Sed circa prædicta quæri potest : Quum Jacobus fuerit primus fidelium Judæorum episcopus, cur non potius ipse quam Petrus, dicitur ordinatus Judæorum apostolus? Et respondendum, quod licet primitivam Ecclesiam rexit in Jerusalem, non tamen sic perambulavit Judæam evangelizando, ut Petrus.
paras.en: [[2:9|And when they had known the grace|Et quum cognovissent gratiam]], that is, the power of miracles, the abundance of wisdom, and the excellence and fitness of preaching, [[2:9|that was given to me|quæ data est mihi]], [[2:9|James|Jacobus]] of Alpheus, the brother of the Lord, [[2:9|and Cephas|et Cephas]], that is, Peter[[John 1:42||]], [[2:9|and John|et Joannes]] the evangelist, [[2:9|who seemed|qui videbantur]], that is, were surely known and seen, [[2:9|to be pillars|columnæ esse]], that is, by their perfection to support the weakness of others, to establish the Church, and to shine before all, [[2:9|gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship|dexteras dederunt mihi et Barnabæ societatis]], that is, received us into their fellowship, and as a sign of companionship and apostolic communion joined their right hands to ours, [[2:9|that we should go unto the Gentiles|ut nos in gentes]] to preach, [[2:9|and they unto the circumcision|ipsi autem in circumcisionem]], that is, among the Jews. [[2:10|Only|Tantum]], that is, this alone they added, [[2:10|that we should be mindful of the poor|ut pauperum memores essemus]], who, selling all they had, laid the price before the Apostles[[Acts 4:34||]][[Acts 4:35||]] [the margin seems to read Act. iv, 34, 35], and afterwards, when a famine arose, were in great want. So the Apostles asked Paul and Barnabas to exhort the converted Gentiles to help these poor. [[2:10|which same thing also I was careful to do|Quod etiam sollicitus fui hoc ipsum facere]], that is, to carry this charge into effect, inducing the Gentiles to send alms to these needy. For it is plain in various epistles how careful Paul was about the collections[[Rom 15:25||]][[1 Cor 16:1||]][[2 Cor 8:9||]] [the margin gives Rom. xv, 25–27; I Cor. xvi, 1, 2; II Cor. viii, ix, etc.]. But about the foregoing it may be asked: Since James was the first bishop of the faithful Jews, why is not he rather than Peter said to be appointed apostle of the Jews? It must be answered that, although he ruled the primitive Church in Jerusalem, he did not travel through Judea preaching the gospel as Peter did.

paras.t: Quum autem venisset Cephas, id est Petrus, Antiochiam, urbem gentilium ; in faciem, id est manifeste, ei restiti, quia in veritatis evangelicæ defensione par ei fui, quia reprehensibilis erat, incaute agendo. Prius enim quam venirent quidam ex Judæis conversi, missi a Jacobo Antiochiam, cum gentibus conversis edebat, non discernens inter cibos ; quum autem venissent prædicti fratres a Jacobo, æmulatores legis, qui Christum et legem æquo jure venerabantur, subtrahebat et segregabat se Petrus a cibo et consortio gentium, timens offendere aut scandalizare eos qui ex circumcisione erant, id est ex populo Judæorum, nisi se hoc modo subtraxisset, et fratribus a Jacobo missis adjunxisset, gentibus derelictis. Et simulationi ejus, videlicet Petri, qua se simulavit servare legalia, tanquam necessaria ad salutem, quum tamen ita non servaret ea (simulavit enim se idem sentire cum fratribus a Jacobo missis : qui etiam erraverunt, putantes legalia de necessitate servanda ; sed Petrus conformavit se eis, ut eos paulatim corrigeret), consenserunt ceteri Judæi conversi ad Christum, Antiochiæ demorantes, vitando cibos et comestionem gentilium, ita ut Barnabas, qui mecum erat ordinatus gentium apostolus, duceretur ab eis, id est a Petro et Judæis Antiochenis, in illam simulationem, cujus exemplum vidit in Petro. Nam licet Antiocheni isti et Barnabas, tanquam viri perfecti, bene sentirent de legalium cessatione, eadem tamen intentione se gentibus subtraxerunt et fratribus a Jacobo venientibus conformaverunt, qua et Petrus. Hæc autem indiscreta simulatio gentes scandalizavit, judaizareque fecit, quoniam gentes his visis, arbitrabantur legalia necessario servanda. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[2:11|But when Cephas was come|Quum autem venisset Cephas]], that is, Peter, [[2:11|to Antioch|Antiochiam]], a city of the Gentiles, [[2:11|I withstood him to the face|in faciem ei restiti]], that is, openly, since in defence of the gospel truth I was his equal, [[2:11|because he was to be blamed|quia reprehensibilis erat]], acting incautiously. [[2:12|For before that some came|Prius enim quam venirent quidam]] of the converted Jews, sent [[2:12|from James|a Jacobo]] to Antioch, [[2:12|he did eat with the Gentiles|cum gentibus conversis edebat]] who were converted, making no distinction of foods; [[2:12|but when they were come|quum autem venissent]], these brethren from James, zealots of the law, who venerated Christ and the law with equal right, [[2:12|he withdrew and separated himself|subtrahebat et segregabat se]], Peter, from the food and company of the Gentiles, [[2:12|fearing|timens]] to offend or scandalize [[2:12|them who were of the circumcision|eos qui ex circumcisione erant]], that is, of the Jewish people, if he had not withdrawn in this way and joined himself to the brethren sent by James, leaving the Gentiles. [[2:13|And to his dissimulation|Et simulationi ejus]], that is, Peter's, by which he pretended to keep the legal ceremonies as necessary to salvation, though he did not keep them so (for he pretended to think the same as the brethren sent by James, who erred, thinking the legal ceremonies must of necessity be kept; but Peter conformed himself to them in order to correct them little by little), [[2:13|the rest of the Jews consented|consenserunt ceteri Judæi]] who were converted to Christ and living at Antioch, avoiding the food and table of the Gentiles, [[2:13|so that Barnabas|ita ut Barnabas]], who had been appointed with me apostle of the Gentiles[[Acts 13:2||]][[Acts 13:3||]] [the margin gives Act. xiii, 2, 3], [[2:13|was led by them|duceretur ab eis]], that is, by Peter and the Jews of Antioch, [[2:13|into that dissimulation|in illam simulationem]], whose example he saw in Peter. For although these men of Antioch and Barnabas, as perfect men, rightly held that the legal ceremonies had ceased, yet they withdrew from the Gentiles and conformed themselves to the brethren coming from James with the same intention as Peter. But this indiscreet dissimulation scandalized the Gentiles and made them judaize, since the Gentiles, seeing this, supposed that the legal ceremonies had necessarily to be kept. Therefore he adds:

paras.t: Sed quum vidissem ego Paulus, quod non recte ambularent, id est, non juste nec vere conversarentur, ad veritatem Evangelii, id est secundum evangelicæ veritatis tenorem : nam propter scandalum evitandum omiserunt veritatem doctrinæ novæ legis, secundum quam legalia cessarunt post Christi passionem, quantum ad obligationem et meritum ; dixi Cephæ tanquam principali, coram omnibus, quoniam manifeste fecit id pro quo corripi meruit, ut et ejus correptione ceteri sanarentur, gentes quoque veritatem cognoscerent : Si, pro Quia, tu, Petre, quum Judæus sis natione, gentiliter et non Judaice, id est, secundum ritum et usum gentium conversaris, non Judæorum, vivis, non discernendo cibos, nec vitando gentiles communiter, quum hac vice aliter agas, quomodo, id est qua ratione, gentes conversas cogis judaizare, id est legales cærimonias observare? Cogis, inquam, tuæ conversationis exemplo, quamvis non cogas doctrinæ imperio.
paras.en: [[2:14|But when I saw|Sed quum vidissem]], I Paul, [[2:14|that they walked not uprightly|quod non recte ambularent]], that is, did not live justly or truly, [[2:14|unto the truth of the gospel|ad veritatem Evangelii]], that is, according to the tenor of the gospel truth: for to avoid scandal they let go the truth of the doctrine of the new law, according to which the legal ceremonies ceased after Christ's passion as regards obligation and merit; [[2:14|I said to Cephas|dixi Cephæ]], as the chief, [[2:14|before them all|coram omnibus]], because he had openly done that for which he deserved to be rebuked, so that by his correction the rest might be healed and the Gentiles also might know the truth: [[2:14|If thou|Si, pro Quia, tu]] (*if* standing for *since*), Peter, [[2:14|being a Jew|quum Judæus sis]] by nation, [[2:14|livest after the manner of the Gentiles and not as the Jews do|vivis, et non judaice]], that is, according to the rite and usage of the Gentiles, not of the Jews, not distinguishing foods nor commonly avoiding the Gentiles, while on this occasion thou actest otherwise, [[2:14|how|quomodo]], that is, for what reason, [[2:14|dost thou compel the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?|gentes conversas cogis judaizare]], the converted Gentiles, that is, to observe the legal ceremonies? Thou compellest, I say, by the example of thy conduct, although thou dost not compel by the command of doctrine.

paras.t: Dicit S. Hieronymus : Hunc locum nobis objecit Porphyrius, arguens Petrum de vitioso errore, et Paulum de procaci increpatione, imo nos omnes devicti dogmatis mendacio, dum inter se principes Ecclesiarum discordant. Unde ad satisfaciendum Porphyrio, et ad excusandum Petrum a culpa, Paulum quoque a præsumptione, Hieronymus dixit, quod Petrus non vere neque ex animo post Christi passionem observavit legalia, sed solum quadam pia simulatione ac dispensatione, ad vitandum scandalum Judæorum. Sicque in prædicta subtractione et judaizatione Petri, erat simulatio in facto et apparentia. Et idem dicit Hieronymus de aliis Apostolis, qui post dominicam passionem legalia observasse leguntur. Asserit namque B. Hieronymus, quod legalia statim post Christi passionem omnibus erant mortifera quibus gratia novi Testamenti fuerat publicata, si ea veraciter observarent : ad quod multas auctoritates et rationes adducit. Insuper dicit Hieronymus, quod Paulus non vere, sed dispensatoria simulatione reprehendit Petrum, quia nec Petrus vere reprehensibilis fuit, ut dicit : ita quod Paulus et Petrus condixerant sibi, ut Petrus se hoc modo a gentibus subtraheret et Judæis misceret, atque ob id Paulus eum argueret, ut videntes gentes tantum Apostolum reprehendi, cognoscerent non esse observanda legalia, nec ea servarent.
paras.en: St Jerome says: Porphyry threw this passage at us, accusing Peter of vicious error and Paul of insolent rebuke, and indeed all of us of the falsehood of a refuted doctrine, since the princes of the Churches disagree among themselves. Hence, to answer Porphyry and to clear Peter of fault and Paul of presumption, Jerome said that Peter after Christ's passion did not observe the legal ceremonies truly or from the heart, but only by a kind of pious pretence and dispensation [[that is, a prudent accommodation for others' sake]], to avoid scandal to the Jews. So in this withdrawal and judaizing of Peter there was pretence in deed and appearance. And Jerome says the same of the other Apostles who are read to have observed the legal ceremonies after the Lord's passion. For blessed Jerome asserts that immediately after Christ's passion the legal ceremonies were deadly to all to whom the grace of the New Testament had been published, if they truly observed them; and for this he brings many authorities and arguments. Moreover Jerome says that Paul rebuked Peter not truly but by a pretence of dispensation, since Peter, as he says, was not truly blameworthy: so that Paul and Peter had agreed together that Peter should withdraw from the Gentiles in this way and mix with the Jews, and that Paul should therefore reprove him, so that the Gentiles, seeing so great an Apostle rebuked, might know that the legal ceremonies were not to be observed, and might not keep them.

paras.t: Porro huic positioni Hieronymi Augustinus contradicit, præsertim in tribus. Primo igitur ait, quod Petrus et alii Apostoli post Christi passionem interdum ex certa causa veraciter servaverunt legalia, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum. Unde simulatio Petri, de qua nunc factus est sermo, non est intelligenda quantum ad opus exterius, seu exteriorem experientiam, sed quantum ad cordis intentionem, quoniam simulavit se consentire Judæis, ut expositum est. — Secundo, dicit Augustinus, quod legalia ante Christi passionem viva atque salubria erant, post promulgationem vero evangelicæ legis fuerunt mortua atque mortifera observantibus ea. Sed tempore intermedio mortua erant, ita quod nullum obligabant, nec aliquid profuerunt ; non autem mortifera Judæis conversis, quia sine peccato poterant observare ad tempus, ex rationabili causa, ita tamen ut spem in eis non figerent, quasi alicujus essent virtutis, vel sine eorum observatione non sufficeret gratia Christi ad veritatem salutis ; sed a gentibus conversis nullo modo erant servanda. Lex quippe, ut ait Augustinus, non erat a Judæis subito abjicienda, sicut a gentibus idololatria, ne videretur non fuisse divina. Eratque mater Synagoga cum honore ad tumulum deducenda, non subito obruenda. — Postremo, perhibet Augustinus Petrum a Paulo veraciter reprehensum, ita quod Petrus venialiter peccavit, indiscrete servando legalia coram gentibus, in scandalum earumdem cogens eas judaizare. Quod probat Augustinus per hoc quod Apostoli non debuerunt omittere veritatem doctrinæ propter vitandum scandalum Judæorum ; item, quoniam non est verisimile quod Paulus in epistola ad Galatas aliquid simulatorie scriberet. Rursus, si Petrus vere reprehensibilis non fuit, Paulus nec vere nec juste scripsit, quod in faciem restitit ei quia reprehensibilis erat, et quod non recte ambulavit ad veritatem Evangelii. Si enim in divinis Scripturis inveniatur unum mendacium, tota veritas ejus nutabit. Hinc ergo Ecclesia magis consentit in hac parte dictis Augustini, quam S. Hieronymi.
paras.en: But Augustine contradicts this position of Jerome, chiefly on three points. First, he says that Peter and the other Apostles after Christ's passion sometimes, for a definite reason, truly kept the legal ceremonies, as is clear in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 10:14||]][[Acts 10:28||]][[Acts 11:1||]][[Acts 16:3||]][[Acts 21:26||]]. Hence the dissimulation of Peter now spoken of is to be understood not of the outward deed or outward practice, but of the intention of the heart, since he pretended to agree with the Jews, as has been explained. Secondly, Augustine says that the legal ceremonies before Christ's passion were living and wholesome, but after the promulgation of the gospel law they were dead and deadly to those who observed them. In the intermediate time, however, they were dead, so that they bound no one and profited nothing; but not deadly to converted Jews, since these could observe them for a time without sin, for a reasonable cause, provided they did not set their hope in them, as if they had some power, or as if without their observance the grace of Christ did not suffice for the truth of salvation; but by converted Gentiles they were in no way to be kept. For the law, as Augustine says, was not to be cast off suddenly by the Jews, as idolatry by the Gentiles, lest it seem not to have been divine. And the mother Synagogue was to be brought to the tomb with honour, not suddenly buried. Lastly, Augustine holds that Peter was truly rebuked by Paul, so that Peter sinned venially by indiscreetly keeping the legal ceremonies before the Gentiles, compelling them to judaize to their scandal. Augustine proves this from the fact that the Apostles ought not to have let go the truth of doctrine to avoid scandal to the Jews; also, because it is not likely that Paul wrote anything in pretence in the epistle to the Galatians. Again, if Peter was not truly blameworthy, Paul wrote neither truly nor justly that he withstood him to the face because he was to be blamed, and that he walked not uprightly unto the truth of the Gospel. For if a single lie be found in the divine Scriptures, their whole truth will waver. Hence the Church agrees more on this point with the sayings of Augustine than with those of St Jerome.

paras.t: Ad blasphemias quoque Porphyrii facile est respondere, videlicet quod non derogat evangelicæ legis veritati, quod ejus ministri quandoque venialiter peccaverint, aut in aliquo modico (quod fidem directe non respicit) erraverint : quia in his quæ fidem concernunt, summa concordia est. Increpatio etiam Pauli procax non fuit, sed ex justa libertate processit : quam et Petrus humiliter pertulit, ut discant prælati non indignari dum a subditis seu inferioribus juste corripiuntur. Verumtamen B. Hieronymus super Isaiam quodam loco positionem suam multum seriose, instanter et fortiter stabilire conatur. — De hac vero materia in Glossa plenius continetur.
paras.en: To the blasphemies of Porphyry too it is easy to answer: namely, that it does not detract from the truth of the gospel law that its ministers sometimes sinned venially, or erred in some small matter (which does not directly concern the faith); for in what concerns the faith there is the highest concord. And Paul's rebuke was not insolent, but proceeded from a just freedom; and Peter bore it humbly, that prelates might learn not to be indignant when they are justly corrected by subjects or inferiors. Yet blessed Jerome, in a certain place on Isaias, tries very earnestly, insistently and strongly to establish his position. On this matter more is contained in the Gloss.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus, quod post Christi adventum et Evangelii prædicationem, carnales observantiæ legis cessaverint, eo quod justificatio sit ex fide, non autem ex lege. Nos Apostoli natura, id est naturali origine, Judæi sumus ex semine Patriarcharum prodeuntes, et non ex gentibus sumus, id est de numero et sorte gentilium, peccatores idololatræ ut illæ, quamvis non simus ab omni peccato immunes. Alibi tamen dicit Apostolus : Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum primus ego sum. Sed nunc dicit, Non ex gentibus peccatores, quoniam vitia gentilitatis non contraxerunt. Scientes autem ex revelatione divina et Scripturarum notitia, quod non justificatur homo Judæus aut quicumque alius coram Deo, ex operibus legis dumtaxat, id est per sola opera legis, præsertim cærimonialia, imo nec per opera legis moralia, sine fide, caritate et gratia Christi. Ideo subditur : nisi per fidem Jesu Christi. Fides enim est prima virtus, sine qua impossibile est Deo placere ; nec sine ea unquam aliquis salvatus est. Sicut enim nos salvamur per fidem qua credimus Christum venisse, sic veteres salvabantur per fidem Christi venturi : imo illorum et nostrum una est fides, quamvis sit modo magis expressa. Tres quippe virtutes theologicæ ad salutem requiruntur, et in omnibus electis fuerunt, sicut et gratia gratum faciens. Hinc ergo Et nos Apostoli omnesque Christiani, in Christo Jesu credimus, id est, de Christo fidem ei placentem atque formatam habemus, ut justificemur ex fide Christi, et non ex operibus legis, fide seclusa. Opera autem legis, proprie appellantur carnales observantiæ, seu facta cærimonialia, quia cum lege constituta terminata sunt. Propter quod, id est sequitur quod, ex operibus legis secundum se sumptis, non justificabitur omnis caro, id est nullus homo. Ponit enim partem pro toto, carnem scilicet pro homine.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows that after Christ's coming and the preaching of the Gospel the carnal observances of the law ceased, because justification is by faith, not by the law. [[2:15|We|Nos]] Apostles [[2:15|by nature|natura]], that is, by natural origin, [[2:15|are Jews|Judæi]], sprung from the seed of the Patriarchs, [[2:15|and not of the Gentiles|et non ex gentibus]], that is, of the number and lot of the Gentiles, [[2:15|sinners|peccatores]], idolaters as they are, though we are not free from all sin. Elsewhere indeed the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 1:15|Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the chief|Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum primus ego sum]]. But here he says, Not of the Gentiles, sinners, because they had not contracted the vices of the Gentiles. [[2:16|But knowing|Scientes autem]] by divine revelation and knowledge of the Scriptures [[2:16|that man is not justified|quod non justificatur homo]], whether Jew or any other, before God, [[2:16|by the works of the law|ex operibus legis]] alone, that is, by the works of the law only, especially the ceremonial ones, indeed not even by the moral works of the law, without faith, charity and the grace of Christ. Therefore he adds: [[2:16|but by the faith of Jesus Christ|nisi per fidem Jesu Christi]]. For faith is the first virtue, without which it is impossible to please God[[Heb 11:6||]]; nor has anyone ever been saved without it. For as we are saved by the faith by which we believe that Christ has come, so the ancients were saved by faith in Christ to come; indeed theirs and ours is one faith, though it is now more explicit. For the three theological virtues are required for salvation, and were in all the elect, as was sanctifying grace [[Latin *gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]]. Hence then [[2:16|we also believe in Christ Jesus|et nos in Christo Jesu credimus]], we Apostles and all Christians, that is, we have a faith about Christ that pleases him and is formed [[that is, quickened by charity]], [[2:16|that we may be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the law|ut justificemur ex fide Christi, et non ex operibus legis]], apart from faith. Now *works of the law* properly means the carnal observances or ceremonial deeds, because they were established with the law and have come to an end. [[2:16|because|Propter quod]], that is, it follows that, [[2:16|by the works of the law|ex operibus legis]] taken in themselves [[2:16|no flesh shall be justified|non justificabitur omnis caro]], that is, no man. For he puts the part for the whole, flesh for man.

paras.t: Quod si nos ipsi quærentes, id est cupientes, justificari in Christo, id est in fide et merito Christi, inventi sumus et ipsi peccatores, id est, eo ipso quod quærimus in Christo justitiam adipisci, probati et declarati sumus esse peccatores : aliter enim non quæreremus in alio justificari ; numquid Christus peccati minister est? id est, numquid Christus, qui jussit nos lege relicta ad se confugere, est peccati causa seu ministrator? Quod utique sequeretur, si lex sine fide et gratia Christi posset salvare. Absit, ut Christus dicatur peccati minister, hoc jubendo, quia nec ego peccavi legem deserendo. Si enim quæ destruxi, iterum hæc reædifico, id est, sic opera legis quæ omisi ac reprobavi, rursus assumo et approbo, prævaricatorem me constituo, id est, Deum offendo hoc faciendo. Ego enim per legem evangelicam, legi Mosaicæ mortuus sum, id est, ab ejus observantia liberatus ac mortificatus, ut Deo vivam vita gratiæ in præsenti, et vita gloriæ in futuro, custodiens legem Christi in omnibus sine querela. Lex etenim Christi virtute sacramentorum suorum gratiam conferet, sicque justificat, non autem lex Moysis. — Ea vero quæ hic dicuntur de insufficientia legis scriptæ et efficacia legis novæ, in epistola ad Romanos plenius subtiliusque conscripta atque tractata sunt.
paras.en: [[2:17|But if, while we seek|Quod si nos ipsi quærentes]], we ourselves, that is, desiring, [[2:17|to be justified in Christ|justificari in Christo]], that is, in the faith and merit of Christ, [[2:17|we ourselves also are found sinners|inventi sumus et ipsi peccatores]], that is, by the very fact that we seek to obtain justice in Christ, we are proved and declared to be sinners (for otherwise we would not seek to be justified in another), [[2:17|is Christ then the minister of sin|numquid Christus peccati minister est]]? that is, is Christ, who bade us leave the law and take refuge in him, the cause or minister of sin? This would certainly follow if the law could save without the faith and grace of Christ. [[2:17|God forbid|Absit]] that Christ be called the minister of sin for commanding this; for neither did I sin in leaving the law. [[2:18|For if I build up again the things which I have destroyed|Si enim quæ destruxi, iterum hæc reædifico]], that is, if I thus take up again and approve the works of the law which I abandoned and rejected, [[2:18|I make myself a prevaricator|prævaricatorem me constituo]], that is, I offend God by doing so. [[2:19|For I, through the law|Ego enim per legem]], the gospel law, [[2:19|am dead to the law|legi Mosaicæ mortuus sum]] of Moses, that is, freed and made dead to its observance, [[2:19|that I may live to God|ut Deo vivam]] with the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future, keeping the law of Christ in all things without blame[[Phil 2:1||]] [the margin gives only Philipp. ii; the phrase *sine querela* is at Phil 2:15]. For the law of Christ confers grace by the power of its sacraments, and so justifies; the law of Moses does not. What is said here of the insufficiency of the written law and the efficacy of the new law is written and treated more fully and more subtly in the epistle to the Romans[[Rom 3:1||]] [the margin gives Rom. iii–viii].

paras.t: Christo confixus sum cruci, id est, clavis amoris et piæ compassionis ac cruciformis imitationis, simul cum Christo confixus sum cruci seu propriæ mortificationis labori, sequendo vestigia ejus, prout ipse ait : Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me. Unde et alibi Apostolus : Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Qui autem Christo crucifixo se ipsum conformat, cruci ejus affigitur, et ardor peccati virtute dominicæ crucis in ipso exstinguitur ; habetque carnes divino timore confixas, ne membra sua ad vitia solita extendantur.
paras.en: [[2:19|with Christ I am nailed to the cross|Christo confixus sum cruci]]: that is, with the nails of love, of devout compassion and of cross-shaped imitation, I am nailed together with Christ to the cross, or to the labour of my own mortification, following his footsteps, as he himself says: [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me]]. Hence the Apostle elsewhere: [[Gal 5:24|And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. He who conforms himself to Christ crucified is fastened to his cross, and the heat of sin is quenched in him by the power of the Lord's cross; and he has his flesh pierced through with the fear of God[[Ps 118:120||]], so that his members are not stretched out to their accustomed vices.

paras.t: Vivo autem jam non ego, id est, postquam Christo confixus sum cruci, vivo et non vivo. Vivo enim non solum vita naturæ, sed gratiæ ; non vita humana, sed divina ; non vita carnali, mundana et consueta, sed spirituali, cœliformi ac nova. Ideo subditur : vivit vero in me Christus, id est, non secundum me ipsum vivo seu ago, sed secundum Christi inspirationem, voluntatem atque doctrinam. Christus ergo vivit in me, id est, regnat in anima mea, et possidet me, facitque me in se vivere. Vivere autem, est actum vitalem habere. Amor vero transponit et mutat amantem in amatum. Dum ergo homo in Christi amore succenditur, crescit et perficitur, moritur in semetipso, quia non agit secundum propriam voluntatem, secundum naturalem inclinationem, secundum privatum amorem, sed secundum divinæ caritatis instinctum, et Christi jussionem atque consilium.
paras.en: [[2:20|And I live, now not I|Vivo autem jam non ego]]: that is, since I have been nailed with Christ to the cross, I live and do not live. For I live not only with the life of nature but of grace; not with a human life but a divine; not with a carnal, worldly and accustomed life, but with a spiritual, heavenly and new one. Therefore he adds: [[2:20|but Christ liveth in me|vivit vero in me Christus]], that is, I do not live or act according to myself, but according to the inspiration, will and teaching of Christ. Christ then lives in me, that is, reigns in my soul, possesses me, and makes me live in him. Now to live is to have vital activity. And love transposes and changes the lover into the beloved. So when a man is kindled, grows and is perfected in the love of Christ, he dies in himself, because he does not act according to his own will, his natural inclination, his private love, but according to the impulse of divine charity and the command and counsel of Christ.

paras.t: Quod autem nunc vivo, id est, bene et meritorie ago, in carne hac fragili, in fide vivo Filii Dei, id est, per virtutem fidei Christi ago, non propria potestate, aut legis subsidio. Justus enim ex fide vivit ; qui vero incredulus est, infideliter agit. Qui dilexit me : sicuti ipse protestatur, Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos ; rursusque per Prophetam, In caritate perpetua dilexi te ; et tradidit semetipsum pro me : prout dicit, Ego sum pastor bonus, et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Hinc Propheta : Tradidit, inquit, in mortem animam suam. Ecce quam affectuosissima prorsusque dulcissima verba. Quod enim generaliter pro omnibus factum est, Apostolus propter ardentissimam ad Christum dilectionem, quasi pro se solo, vel singulariter factum æstimat. Nam ut ait Chrysostomus : Hic est affectus servi fidelis, ut quod pro omnibus communiter fecit et pertulit Christus, quasi pro se tantum putet illum fecisse et pertulisse. Et utique merito hoc æstimare debemus, quoniam tanta est Christi misericordia, bonitas, et dilectio ad unumquemque nostrum, ut mallet pro quolibet sigillatim ac singulariter omnia facere et sustinere, quæ pro omnibus simul fecit et passus est, quam aliquem perire, quantum est ex parte ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:20|And that I live now|Quod autem nunc vivo]], that is, act well and meritoriously, [[2:20|in the flesh|in carne]], this frail flesh, [[2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God|in fide vivo Filii Dei]], that is, I act by the power of faith in Christ, not by my own power or the help of the law. For [[Rom 1:17|the just man liveth by faith|Justus enim ex fide vivit]]; but [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|qui vero incredulus est, infideliter agit]]. [[2:20|who loved me|Qui dilexit me]]: as he himself declares, [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]; and again through the Prophet, [[Jer 31:3|I have loved thee with an everlasting love|In caritate perpetua dilexi te]]; [[2:20|and delivered himself for me|et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]: as he says, [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]], [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. Hence the Prophet says: [[Is 53:12|he hath delivered his soul unto death|Tradidit, inquit, in mortem animam suam]]. Behold what most affectionate and altogether most sweet words! For what was done for all in general, the Apostle, out of his most ardent love for Christ, regards as done as it were for himself alone, or singly. For as Chrysostom says: This is the affection of a faithful servant, that what Christ did and suffered for all in common, he should think Christ did and suffered as if for him alone. And rightly ought we to think so, since so great is Christ's mercy, goodness and love towards each one of us, that he would rather do and endure for each one singly and individually all that he did and suffered for all together, than that anyone should perish, as far as lies with him.

paras.t: Non abjicio gratiam Dei, id est, caritatem et beneficia divina mihi per Christum collata, non sperno nec desero, legi finaliter inhærendo. Si enim per legem justitia, id est, si virtute et actibus legis homo justificatur, remissionem peccati et gratiæ infusionem adipiscendo, ut Judæi confidunt, ergo Christus gratis, id est sine causa necessaria, et quasi superflue, mortuus est, quum non sit mortuus, secundum Scripturas, nisi propter hominis justificationem, juxta illud propheticum : Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris.
paras.en: [[2:21|I cast not away the grace of God|Non abjicio gratiam Dei]], that is, I do not spurn or forsake the charity and the divine benefits conferred on me through Christ by clinging finally to the law. [[2:21|For if justice be by the law|Si enim per legem justitia]], that is, if man is justified by the power and acts of the law, obtaining remission of sin and infusion of grace, as the Jews trust, [[2:21|then Christ died in vain|ergo gratis Christus mortuus est]], that is, without necessary cause and as it were superfluously; whereas, according to the Scriptures, he died only for man's justification, according to that prophetic word: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]].
